title: Be Careful Not to Punish Competence
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece names a subtle failure mode where leaders, wanting the best outcomes, keep routing the most important work to the same high-performing team members, effectively punishing competence with an ever-heavier workload. The author traces the emotional arc of this pattern for the affected team member. The piece frames this as often invisible to leaders. The prescribed fix is deliberate work distribution and coaching up other team members, treating the protection of top talent from overload as itself a leadership responsibility.
points: Leaders who repeatedly route the most important work to their best people are punishing competence with an ever-heavier load.
The overloaded high performer's experience follows a predictable arc, initial flattery, then mounting overwhelm, resentment, and eventual burnout.
The imbalance created by over-relying on top talent breeds either resentment or complacency in the rest of the team.
The recommended fix is deliberate: consciously spread assignments more evenly and invest in coaching up other team members.
quotes: Leaders naturally want their highest talent on the most important projects and tasks. But they sometimes go to the well too often.
By leaning so heavily on the same team members, they unintentionally punish them for being highly competent.
At first, this can seem like high recognition. But the continual requests and work soon become overwhelming, potentially creating sourness and burnout.
They coach up others and create more expertise on the team through experience and opportunities for everyone.
Losing high talent because they are overworked and overtasked is never a winning strategy. The best leaders are careful not to punish competence.
